I am an old woman of 64 years here in the South South, and this small plot behind my house is where I plant my yam and cassava. I cannot afford the chemical fertilizer this year — the price has gone too high — so I will use the droppings from my goats and the ash from the kitchen to feed the soil. I will plant the cassava stems and yam setts I kept from last year's harvest, as my mother taught me. My back is not strong anymore, so my daughter-in-law will help me, and I will pay one young man from the village to help with the ridging and weeding.
